title: Desertion as a divorce ground - how long must it actually last
p1: Many people believe that if a spouse leaves the home, divorce can immediately be filed. But the law does not always see physical separation as desertion.
p2: A surprising fact: desertion is not just about living apart. It usually involves leaving the marriage without a valid reason and with the intention of ending the relationship. In India, for example, under the Hindu Marriage Act, desertion generally must continue for at least two years before it becomes a ground for divorce.
p3: The key point is that the timeline alone is not enough. Courts also look at the intention behind the separation, whether there was consent, and whether attempts were made to continue the marriage. A spouse staying away due to work, health reasons, or a temporary dispute may not automatically amount to desertion. The practical takeaway: separation and legal desertion are not the same thing.
conclusion: Did you know that simply living separately does not always qualify as desertion for divorce? What factors do you think should matter most in such cases?
